method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: QUOTED from French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI) 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group' (published 10 June 2024), 26 claims; LICENCE: CC BY 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC11201647). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (Haematology Reference Committee) 'eviQ hairy cell leukaemia protocols (not guidelines): 364 cladribine (v.6, last reviewed 24 February 2023) and 4383 rituximab and cladribine (v.1, last reviewed 8 March 2024)' (retrieved 24 September 2026 (review due: 364 30 June 2027; 4383 30 June 2026)), 9 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0. eviQ also states that "eviQ content should not be hosted on external sites", and that commercial entities must contact eviQ to seek permission (read at https://www.eviq.org.au/copyright (Disclaimer and copyright page)). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 keeps every FILO 2024 claim (S1) unchanged and adds S2, two Australian eviQ protocols (CC BY-NC 4.0, paraphrased), for the local cladribine and cladribine-rituximab schedules, PBS status, premedication and supportive care. The S2 source file concatenates the two protocol pages (https://www.eviq.org.au/p/364 and /p/4383), each under a header line naming its URL; only protocol text from the ID line to the literature-search section was kept. eviQ asks that adaptations cite the eviQ ID, version and URL: 364 v.6 and 4383 v.1, at those URLs. Table rows appended with pmc_text.py --append-tables (2026-09-24); claims from S1 Table 1 (baseline and pretreatment work-up), Table 2 (response criteria), Table 3 (HCL vs HCL-like disorders) and Table 4 (treatment regimens). All four S1 tables were clean.

claims.claim: **HCL is rare (2-3% of leukaemias), mostly in men (5:1)**; median age at diagnosis is 63 in men and 59 in women.
claims.source_text: HCL accounts for 2-3% of all leukemias [,] and fewer than 1% of all hematological disorders. … The male-to-female sex ratio is 5:1. … At diagnosis, the median age is 63 years for men and 59 years for women.
claims.locator: French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI), 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group', published 10 June 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11201647/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **It presents with marrow failure (infections, anaemia, bleeding), a large spleen, or hairy cells found on a routine count.** Lymph nodes and liver are rarely enlarged. About 20% have an opportunistic infection at diagnosis, and autoimmune disease affects about one in four.
claims.source_text: The symptoms of HCL are related to BM failure (severe or recurrent infections, anemia, thrombocytopenia with hemorrhages), spleen involvement or fortuitous identification of HC during a routine complete blood count (CBC). Splenomegaly is common, while hepatomegaly and enlarged lymph nodes are rare. … In about 20% of cases, opportunistic infections occur at diagnosis … Autoimmune disorders are also frequent at diagnosis or during the course of the disease and may occur in one out of four patients.
claims.locator: French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI), 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group', published 10 June 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11201647/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Low monocytes are a clue** that sets HCL apart from look-alike disorders, but analysers often count hairy cells as monocytes and hide it.
claims.source_text: Unlike HCL-like disorders, monocytopenia is often present in HCL: it can be masked by automated hematology analyzers, which frequently identify HCs as monocytes
claims.locator: French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI), 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group', published 10 June 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11201647/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Diagnosis rests on four tests:** blood count with film review, trephine marrow biopsy (aspirates are often dry), multiparameter flow cytometry, and BRAF V600E testing.
claims.source_text: The diagnosis is based on four criteria: (1) complete blood count (CBC) with morphologic assessment, (2) trephine bone marrow biopsy with dry marrow aspirates, (3) multiparametric flow cytometry (FCM) and, (4) identification of the BRAFV600E mutation.
claims.locator: French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI), 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group', published 10 June 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11201647/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Flow cytometry score:** one point each for CD11c, CD25, CD103 and CD123; HCL scores 3 or more in 98% of cases, look-alikes score below 3.
claims.source_text: The four markers CD11c, CD25, CD103 and CD123 define the HCL immunophenotypic score [] (one point is given to each expressed marker), which distinguishes HCL that are ≥3 in 98% of cases from other HCL-like disorders with a low score <3.
claims.locator: French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI), 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group', published 10 June 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11201647/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Test for BRAF V600E at diagnosis** (preferably on marrow aspirate): it is present in over 90% of HCL and usually absent in look-alikes. A karyotype is not recommended because it does not change treatment.
claims.source_text: We do not recommend performing a karyotype at diagnosis of HCL, even if it may show several abnormalities. In fact, the presence or absence of these abnormalities will not modify the type of treatment. … We recommend BRAF testing for diagnosis. BRAF testing should be carried out whenever possible in the BM aspirate. The BRAFV600E mutation is present in more than 90% of HCL [] and is usually absent in HCL-like disorders.
claims.locator: French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI), 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group', published 10 June 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11201647/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Extra molecular tests (S1 Table 1):** IGHV repertoire and mutation status if BRAF is wild-type or at relapse; an extended panel (BRAF exons 11 and 15, MAP2K1, KRAS, NRAS, HRAS) if BRAF is wild-type; TP53 at relapse or refractory disease.
claims.source_text: [Table 1 row 6] Diagnosis: IGHV repertory and mutational status · General Practice: Recommended if BRAF WT or if R/R cases … [Table 1 row 7] Diagnosis: Extended mutational landscape (BRAF exon 11 and 15, MAP2K1, KRAS, NRAS, HRAS) · General Practice: Recommended if BRAF WT … [Table 1 row 8] Diagnosis: TP53 mutational status · General Practice: Recommended if R/R cases
claims.locator: French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI), 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group', published 10 June 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11201647/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pretreatment work-up for everyone (S1 Table 1):** history and examination with performance status, creatinine clearance, direct antiglobulin test, haptoglobin, unconjugated bilirubin and LDH, transaminases, and hepatitis B and C serology. A chest radiograph or CT (chest, abdomen, pelvis), stored cells and serum, and MRD assessment are recommended; keep MRI or PET-CT for symptomatic patients with unusual extramedullary sites.
claims.source_text: [Table 1 row 11] Diagnosis: History, physical examination (performans status) · General Practice: All cases [Table 1 row 12] Diagnosis: Creatinine clearance · General Practice: All cases [Table 1 row 13] Diagnosis: Direct antiglobulin test, haptoglobin, unconjugated bilirubin and lactic dehydrogenase · General Practice: All cases [Table 1 row 14] Diagnosis: Transaminases, hepatitis B and C serology · General Practice: All cases [Table 1 row 15] Diagnosis: Preservation of cells and serum in a tumor bank · General Practice: Recommended [Table 1 row 16] Diagnosis: Chest radiograph or CT scan (chest abdomen and pelvis) · General Practice: Recommended [Table 1 row 17] Diagnosis: MRI/PET CT scan · General Practice: In symptomatic patients with unusual extramedullary localizations [Table 1 row 18] Diagnosis: Assessment for MRD · General Practice: Recommended
claims.locator: French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI), 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group', published 10 June 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11201647/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Telling HCL from look-alikes (S1 Table 3):** only HCL has low monocytes, bright CD25 and CD200, and annexin A1 and VE1 (BRAF V600E) staining. HCL variant has constant prominent nucleoli, marked lymphocytosis (90% or more), is CD25-negative in over 90%, and has no BRAF V600E (0%); splenic diffuse red pulp lymphoma and splenic marginal zone lymphoma are also almost always BRAF V600E-negative (0–2%).
claims.source_text: [Table 3 row 8] Monocytopenia · HCL: Yes · HCLv: No · SDRPL: No · SZML: No … [Table 3 row 9] Lymphocytosis · HCL: ≤10% · HCLv: ≥90% · SDRPL: ≥50% · SZML: ≥50% … [Table 3 row 11] Nucleoli · HCL: Occasional, inconspicuous · HCLv: Constant, prominent · SDRPL: Occasional · SZML: Small … [Table 3 row 16] CD25 · HCL: +Bright · HCLv: -(>90%) · SDRPL: -(>90%) · SZML: -(78-88%) … [Table 3 row 21] CD200 · HCL: +Bright · HCLv: - · SDRPL: - · SZML: - … [Table 3 row 24] Immunohistochemistry · Annexin A1 · HCL: + · HCLv: - · SDRPL: - · SZML: - … [Table 3 row 26] VE 1 · HCL: + · HCLv: - · SDRPL: - · SZML: - … [Table 3 row 34] BRAF V600E · HCL: 70-100% · HCLv: 0% · SDRPL: 0-2% · SZML: 0-2%
claims.locator: French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI), 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group', published 10 June 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11201647/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat only when a criterion is met:** Hb below 11 g/dL, platelets below 100 G/L or neutrophils below 1 G/L; symptomatic organomegaly; constitutional symptoms; or recurrent infections. Otherwise watch and wait.
claims.source_text: HCL and HCL-like disorders should be treated only if one or more of the following criteria are present: (1) Hb < 11 g/dL and/or platelets < 100 G/L and/or neutrophils < 1 G/L, (2) symptomatic organomegaly, (3) constitutional symptoms (fever, weight loss, night sweats), (4) recurrent infections. If none of these criteria are present, we recommend a 'watch and wait' strategy.
claims.locator: French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI), 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group', published 10 June 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11201647/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Delay treatment until an active infection is controlled.** If that is not possible, bridge with low-dose BRAF inhibitor (not myelosuppressive), then switch to cladribine plus rituximab.
claims.source_text: In case of active infection, we recommend to delay the start of HCL treatment until infection is controlled. If delaying the start of treatment is not possible, the use of a bridging therapy with low-dose BRAFi is our recommendation due to the absence of myelotoxic and myelosuppressive effects. … Once infection is controlled, a switch to CDA + R is recommended.
claims.locator: French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI), 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group', published 10 June 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11201647/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Fit patients: cladribine plus rituximab, given together** (rituximab from day 1 of cladribine, 8 weekly infusions). This beat purine analogue alone and the sequential schedule; response and CR were both 100%, with 97% reaching undetectable MRD.
claims.source_text: In first-line and fit patients, we recommend CDAR regimen with CDA plus rituximab (R). The data with P plus rituximab are limited []. CDA plus R was demonstrated to be more effective than PNA in monotherapy, allowing to reach undetectable MRD (uMRD) in most patients and to achieve more durable responses. … The simultaneous combination of R + CDA (i.e., R started at day 1 of CDA) was shown to be superior to the sequential schedule of CDA followed by R (i.e., R started 6 months later). R is given at day 1 of CDA for 8 weekly infusions []. The overall response rate (ORR) and the CR rate were both 100%, with 97% of patients reaching uMRD.
claims.locator: French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI), 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group', published 10 June 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11201647/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Cladribine dose:** subcutaneous 0.1-0.14 mg/kg/day once daily for 5 days is preferred over IV 0.1 mg/kg/day by continuous infusion for 7 days.
claims.source_text: The subcutaneous (SC) formulation of CDA (0.1-0.14 mg/kg/d once per day for 5 days) is favored as compared to the intravenous (iv) formulation (0.1 mg/kg/d as continuous intravenous infusion for 7 days)
claims.locator: French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI), 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group', published 10 June 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11201647/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A purine analogue alone remains an option and can give durable responses.** Pentostatin is 4 mg/m² IV every 2 weeks for one year; stop it and reconsider if there is no response at 6 months.
claims.source_text: PNAs in monotherapy remain an option as the patients may achieve a durable response even if they do not reach uMRD. … Pentostatin is given intravenously at 4 mg/m2 once every 2 weeks for one year. If there is no response at 6 months, P should be stopped and another treatment should be discussed
claims.locator: French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI), 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group', published 10 June 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11201647/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Unfit or very elderly patients:** purine analogue alone, or two or three days of subcutaneous cladribine instead of five. If unfit even for that, a BRAF inhibitor with or without rituximab, or interferon alfa. Rituximab alone is not recommended.
claims.source_text: For unfit patients not able to receive CDA + R, PNA in monotherapy is a good option. Two or three days (instead of five) of subcutaneous CDA may be used in very elderly people. If patients are unfit to receive PNA alone, BRAFi +/- R or IFNα are alternative choices [,]. R alone is not recommended because responses are partial and short-lasting
claims.locator: French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI), 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group', published 10 June 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11201647/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Kidney function:** cladribine is contraindicated at creatinine clearance of 50 mL/min or less, and pentostatin below 60 mL/min. Vemurafenib is an alternative if BRAF is mutated.
claims.source_text: In case of renal insufficiency, CDA is contra-indicated if clearance is ≤ 50 mL/min and P if clearance is < 60 mL/min because of a lack of data and a potential risk of increased toxicity … alternatively, if BRAF is mutated, vemurafenib could be used.
claims.locator: French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI), 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group', published 10 June 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11201647/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In pregnancy, delay treatment until after delivery;** if that is not possible, interferon alfa is preferred.
claims.source_text: In the rare case of HCL occurring during pregnancy, we recommend delaying treatment until after childbirth. If delaying HCL therapy is not possible, use of IFNα is preferable.
claims.locator: French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI), 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group', published 10 June 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11201647/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: 🇦🇺 **Australian protocol (eviQ ID 364): cladribine 0.14 mg/kg by IV infusion over 2 hours on days 1 to 5, as one course.** Most patients respond to that single course; if another is needed, wait until every blood-count toxicity has recovered. eviQ lists cladribine as PBS Authority.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (Haematology Reference Committee), 'eviQ hairy cell leukaemia protocols (not guidelines): 364 cladribine (v.6, last reviewed 24 February 2023) and 4383 rituximab and cladribine (v.1, last reviewed 8 March 2024)', retrieved 24 September 2026 (review due: 364 30 June 2027; 4383 30 June 2026), https://www.eviq.org.au/haematology/leukaemias/hairy-cell-leukaemia, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **eviQ accepts four published cladribine schedules as reasonable:** 0.1 mg/kg/day by continuous IV infusion for seven days; 0.14 mg/kg/day IV over 2 hours for five days; 0.15 mg/kg IV over 2 hours weekly for six weeks; or 0.085 mg/kg/day subcutaneously for seven days. It picked the 5-day IV schedule because it fits outpatient care in a short, fixed window.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (Haematology Reference Committee), 'eviQ hairy cell leukaemia protocols (not guidelines): 364 cladribine (v.6, last reviewed 24 February 2023) and 4383 rituximab and cladribine (v.1, last reviewed 8 March 2024)', retrieved 24 September 2026 (review due: 364 30 June 2027; 4383 30 June 2026), https://www.eviq.org.au/haematology/leukaemias/hairy-cell-leukaemia, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: 🇦🇺 **Australian cladribine-rituximab protocol (eviQ ID 4383; HCL and HCL variant): rituximab 375 mg/m² IV on days 1, 8, 15, 22, 29, 36, 43 and 50, with cladribine 0.14 mg/kg IV on days 1 to 5, as one cycle.** eviQ flags it as resting on limited evidence, notes that the cladribine schedule and number of rituximab doses differ between studies, and lists rituximab on the PBS general schedule.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (Haematology Reference Committee), 'eviQ hairy cell leukaemia protocols (not guidelines): 364 cladribine (v.6, last reviewed 24 February 2023) and 4383 rituximab and cladribine (v.1, last reviewed 8 March 2024)', retrieved 24 September 2026 (review due: 364 30 June 2027; 4383 30 June 2026), https://www.eviq.org.au/haematology/leukaemias/hairy-cell-leukaemia, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Rituximab carries a high risk of infusion reactions.** eviQ's default premedication, 60 minutes before each dose, is oral paracetamol 1,000 mg and loratadine 10 mg with IV hydrocortisone 100 mg; consider holding antihypertensives around the infusion because blood pressure can fall.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (Haematology Reference Committee), 'eviQ hairy cell leukaemia protocols (not guidelines): 364 cladribine (v.6, last reviewed 24 February 2023) and 4383 rituximab and cladribine (v.1, last reviewed 8 March 2024)', retrieved 24 September 2026 (review due: 364 30 June 2027; 4383 30 June 2026), https://www.eviq.org.au/haematology/leukaemias/hairy-cell-leukaemia, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Kidney function (eviQ):** there are too few data to set a cladribine dose change for kidney impairment, so treat known or suspected impairment cautiously and monitor regularly for toxicity.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (Haematology Reference Committee), 'eviQ hairy cell leukaemia protocols (not guidelines): 364 cladribine (v.6, last reviewed 24 February 2023) and 4383 rituximab and cladribine (v.1, last reviewed 8 March 2024)', retrieved 24 September 2026 (review due: 364 30 June 2027; 4383 30 June 2026), https://www.eviq.org.au/haematology/leukaemias/hairy-cell-leukaemia, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **At relapse, repeat the full work-up** (examination, blood count, trephine, flow cytometry) and retest BRAF, IGHV status, VH4-34 use and TP53, which carry prognostic weight.
claims.source_text: In case of relapse, a new complete work-up is needed, including a complete physical examination, CBC, trephine BM biopsy, and FCM. We also recommend BRAF testing again, the study of IGHV mutational profile, use or not of the VH4-34 repertory and the TP53 status. UM IGHV, VH4-34 usage and TP53 alterations confer an unfavorable prognosis in HCL
claims.locator: French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI), 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group', published 10 June 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11201647/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Choice by length of first response:** more than five years and fit, repeat cladribine plus rituximab; two to five years, choose between cladribine plus rituximab and vemurafenib plus rituximab; primary refractory or under two years, vemurafenib plus rituximab.
claims.source_text: In case of response lasting more than five years and if the patient is fit, a treatment combining a CDAR is recommended again. … In case of response between two and five years, the different options should be considered based on the number and severity of associated comorbidities and clinician judgment. The options to be discussed are CDA plus R or vemurafenib plus R. … In case of primary refractory disease or in case of short response lasting less than two years after first-line therapy, we recommend the use of vemurafenib plus R.
claims.locator: French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI), 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group', published 10 June 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11201647/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Vemurafenib plus rituximab** (off-label; in a single-centre trial, vemurafenib 960 mg twice daily for 8 weeks, rituximab 375 mg/m² for eight infusions over 18 weeks) gave response and CR of 87%. Watch for skin cancers, joint, eye, pancreatic and liver toxicity, and monitor the ECG for QT prolongation.
claims.source_text: vemurafenib was given at 960 mg twice daily for 8 weeks and R at 375 mg/m2 for eight infusions over 18 weeks (started at day 1 of vemurafenib). The ORR and CR rate were both 87% … Practitioners must be aware of cutaneous (rash, photosensitivity, basal-cell carcinoma, squamous-cell carcinoma, melanoma), articular (arthralgia, arthritis), ocular, pancreatic and hepatic (elevation of lipasemia and transaminitis) adverse events. Electrocardiogram (ECG) must be regularly performed because of possible prolongation of the QT interval.
claims.locator: French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI), 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group', published 10 June 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11201647/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Other relapse options:** dabrafenib 150 mg twice daily with trametinib 2 mg daily; moxetumomab where still available. Beyond the third line, avoid further purine analogue, and use ibrutinib or venetoclax (with or without rituximab) after BRAF-inhibitor exposure.
claims.source_text: 55 R/R HCL patients received continuous dabrafenib 150 mg twice daily with trametinib 2 mg once daily until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. … In countries where it is available, Moxe is a good alternative option … In patients in third line and beyond, we do not recommend the use of PNA again, especially if recurrence of HCL has occurred within 2-5 years. … If patients have previously received BRAFi, we recommend ibrutinib, or venetoclax +/- R
claims.locator: French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI), 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group', published 10 June 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11201647/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Other regimen doses (S1 Table 4):** vemurafenib alone 960 mg twice daily for 16–18 weeks; trametinib alone 2 mg once daily until progression or unacceptable toxicity; moxetumomab pasudotox 40 µg/kg IV on days 1, 3 and 5, up to six 28-day cycles; ibrutinib 420 mg/d or 840 mg/d until progression or toxicity; venetoclax 400 mg/d after a ramp-up, for at most 12 28-day cycles; bendamustine 90 mg/m² IV on days 1 and 2 with rituximab 375 mg/m² on day 1, for 6 28-day cycles.

claims.claim: **Response criteria (S1 Table 2):** complete response needs the spleen to regress on examination, near-normal counts without transfusion (Hb above 11 g/dL, platelets above 100 G/L, neutrophils above 1.5 G/L) and no hairy cells in blood or marrow; partial response needs at least 50% regression of spleen size and of marrow infiltration with the same counts. Progression is a rise of at least 25% in spleen size and/or a fall of at least 25% in blood counts, and/or worsening symptoms.
claims.source_text: [Table 2 row 1] Response: Complete response (CR) · Definition: Regression of splenomegaly on physical examination. Near normalization of blood count without transfusion: Hb > 11 g/dL, platelets > 100 G/L, neutrophils > 1.5 G/L. Absence of hairy-cell on blood smear and bone marrow examination. … [Table 2 row 3] Response: Partial response (PR) · Definition: Regression of at least 50% of splenomegaly on physical examination. Near normalization of blood count without transfusion: Hb > 11 g/dL, platelets > 100 G/L, neutrophils > 1.5 G/L. Regression of at least 50% of bone marrow infiltration by hairy cells. … [Table 2 row 5] Response: Progressive disease (PD) · Definition: Increase of at least 25% of splenomegaly on physical examination and/or decline of at least 25% of hematological parameters and/or increase of symptoms.
claims.locator: French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI), 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group', published 10 June 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11201647/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **After treatment, give Pneumocystis prophylaxis (cotrimoxazole) and herpes zoster prophylaxis (valaciclovir or aciclovir)** for at least six months and until CD4 exceeds 0.2 G/L. With purine analogues, start them two weeks after the analogue because of skin reactions.
claims.source_text: For patients who have received a treatment for HCL or HCL-like disorder, we recommend a prophylaxis against Pneumocystis jirovecii with cotrimoxazole, and a prophylaxis against zona and herpes zoster viruses with valaciclovir or aciclovir. When PNAs are used, we recommend starting these molecules two weeks after initiation of PNAs, because of possible cutaneous adverse events. Prophylaxis must be continued for at least six months and until the CD4+ T-cell count is >0.2 G/L.
claims.locator: French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI), 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group', published 10 June 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11201647/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Use G-CSF with broad-spectrum antibiotics for febrile neutropenia.** Vaccinate against influenza, SARS-CoV-2 and pneumococcus before treatment where possible, and consider irradiated blood products after purine analogues.
claims.source_text: In case of transfusion for a patient who has received PNAs, irradiation of the blood products could be discussed. We recommend the use of G-CSF in case of febrile neutropenia, in combination with large-spectrum antibiotics. Vaccines against influenza, SARS-CoV-2, and Streptococcus pneumoniae should ideally be realized before starting treatment if possible, especially in elderly patients with comorbidities.
claims.locator: French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI), 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group', published 10 June 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11201647/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Second cancers, especially skin cancers, are common in HCL whatever the treatment:** arrange a full skin check with a dermatologist at least yearly.
claims.source_text: Prevention of second primary malignancies, especially cutaneous cancers, is recommended because of the high risk of second cancers in HCL patients, regardless of the treatment received [,]. We recommend a regular (at least once a year) complete physical examination with a dermatologist.
claims.locator: French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) and French-speaking experts (Troussard X, Maitre E, Paillassa J, et al.), Cancers (MDPI), 'Recommendations for the Management of Patients with Hairy-Cell Leukemia and Hairy-Cell Leukemia-like Disorders: A Work by French-Speaking Experts and French Innovative Leukemia Organization (FILO) Group', published 10 June 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11201647/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Cladribine depletes CD4 and CD8 T cells deeply and for a long time, so expect more opportunistic infections during treatment and for six months afterwards** (eviQ). It recommends antimicrobial prophylaxis; Pneumocystis prophylaxis is left to the treating clinician (for example trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 160/800 mg, one tablet twice a day on two days each week, or one tablet on three days each week), and antiviral prophylaxis should be considered, above all with lymphopenia.

claims.claim: **Tumour lysis (eviQ):** assess each patient's risk; allopurinol 100 mg by mouth once a day, from the first treatment day for 2 weeks, is recommended.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (Haematology Reference Committee), 'eviQ hairy cell leukaemia protocols (not guidelines): 364 cladribine (v.6, last reviewed 24 February 2023) and 4383 rituximab and cladribine (v.1, last reviewed 8 March 2024)', retrieved 24 September 2026 (review due: 364 30 June 2027; 4383 30 June 2026), https://www.eviq.org.au/haematology/leukaemias/hairy-cell-leukaemia, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Blood tests (eviQ):** check FBC, EUC, eGFR and LFTs before starting, and the FBC every week during and after treatment; myelosuppression is severe, so watch counts closely for the first 4 to 8 weeks. Postpone further treatment while neutrophils are below 1.5 or platelets below 100 unless the leukaemia itself is the cause.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (Haematology Reference Committee), 'eviQ hairy cell leukaemia protocols (not guidelines): 364 cladribine (v.6, last reviewed 24 February 2023) and 4383 rituximab and cladribine (v.1, last reviewed 8 March 2024)', retrieved 24 September 2026 (review due: 364 30 June 2027; 4383 30 June 2026), https://www.eviq.org.au/haematology/leukaemias/hairy-cell-leukaemia, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Also before and during treatment (eviQ):** use irradiated blood components; screen for hepatitis B (HBsAg, anti-HBc and anti-HBs) first; avoid live vaccines; and watch for new neurological symptoms, since progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy has been reported.
